findings.finding: The confirmed FY-26 standalone adj. EBIT guide of EUR3.4bn sits above the street's path: H1 actual 1,772m plus the company-compiled Q3 consensus of 866m leaves 762m for Q4, only +4.5% on Q4-25's 729m (FY-25 3,245m less 9M-25 2,516m), so the quarter at or above consensus with the guide reiterated (or nudged) is the base case, a mild beat lean.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1-26: EBIT +13.6% with the guide raised to 3.4bn and the stock rallied (teleborsa 2026-05-07); Q2-26: EBIT 868m beat the 857.6m consensus with the guide confirmed and the stock fell 3.65% on 24 Jul (baseline tape, release 07:00 that day). Beats alone have been sold; the move came with the guide change.
findings.original_quote: Il risultato operativo adjusted è previsto a 866 milioni di euro (856 milioni nel 3° trimestre 2025), con un minimo di 800 milioni e un massimo di 915 milioni di euro [Adjusted operating profit is expected at EUR866m (856m in Q3 2025), range 800-915m]
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the guide and consensus are both public and 16+ analysts cover the name. What is not in the price is only the small gap between the 3.4bn guide and a consensus that implies roughly 3.37bn; if the market priced a guide raise the stock would not sit about 12% below its July high of over EUR29 (H1 release) at 25.5.
findings.independence: Guide from the company's own H1 release (https://www.emarketstorage.com/sites/default/files/comunicati/2026-07/20260724_187167.pdf); Q2 beat vs Bloomberg consensus reported by FinanzaOnline (https://www.finanzaonline.com/?p=782376). Both are the company's own trajectory, not an independent series.

findings.finding: Industry proxy for Poste Vita flows is mixed: ANIA life new business in August 2026 was EUR6.3bn (+4.4% y/y incl. EU companies) while the bank and post-office counter channel collected EUR3.9bn, -0.9% y/y; Poste's insurance EBIT is driven by CSM release, so the transmission to the quarter is weak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Insurance was the line that beat in Q2-26 (websim: '2Q26 leggermente sopra le attese sull'Insurance') and the stock still fell 3.65%.
findings.original_quote: ad agosto ha raggiunto 6,3 miliardi di euro [in August it reached EUR6.3bn]
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced to the extent it matters: an industry series with a channel that mixes banks and Poste, and a flat-to-down counter channel against a positive total. A real signal would show as a consensus revision in the insurance segment, and there is none visible.
findings.independence: Counter-channel -0.9% figure from search summary of ANIA data (snippet_only, not opened in document); none independent.

findings.finding: The stock runs into the print up 5.45% in five sessions (+4.25% over 20) after selling its last beat-and-confirm print by 3.65%, so a reiterated guide meets a market that has bought ahead of it.

baseline_tension: The mild beat lean cuts slightly against the negative run-up lean, but the strong five-day run-up and a sold Q2 beat agree with it, so the two roughly cancel.
language_note: The company-compiled Q3 consensus (adj. EBIT 866m, range 800-915; net profit ex-TIM 598m) came only from an Italian source (SoldiOnline); English searches returned no Q3 bar.

The release timing came from Italian-language eMarket STORAGE notices ('Data/Ora Inizio Diffusione') and a Websim note ('Poste pubblicherà i risultati del terzo trimestre giovedì prima dell'apertura'); English calendars disagreed (10, 11 and 12 Nov).

lessons_applied: 'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with': the run-up finding partly restates the priced lean, so it was cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
